literal_reason: The Original u1/u2 correctly aim at broad search and anti-cycling, but current executions show the same failure pattern persists. In P1 the Actor only reaches the box on coffeetable 1 at P1:36 after cycling through empty cabinets and drawers from P1:15 onward. P3 and P6 hit the step limit: P3 repeatedly cycles cabinets and countertop, and P6 repeatedly revisits empty drawers, dresser, and sidetables while never testing diningtable, sofa, armchair, ottoman, or other listed surfaces. Historical Memory M3, M6, and M9 independently report that preference-style anti-revisit wording was not reliably followed and did not break cycling. I therefore replace the preference wording with two executable local rules. u1 makes the container/non-container distinction explicit and forbids two consecutive container go-to actions. u2 confines anti-revisit and diversity to what the Actor can see in the current and last two observations. This is a testable behavioral hypothesis, not a proven improvement; P3/P6 may also lack the exact target, and one trial per task limits attribution. Exact-target/no-substitute, cleaning/cooling/heat, placement, and desklamp co-location remain covered outside these Updates.

applied_text_for_diagnostic_only.u1:
- When the exact requested target has not yet been acquired, search by receptacle type using the admissible `go to` list, and avoid long runs of the same category.
- Classify cabinet, drawer, fridge, and microwave as closed containers requiring an open action; classify diningtable, coffeetable, sidetable, sofa, armchair, bed, dresser, countertop, stoveburner, sinkbasin, toaster, and coffeemachine as non-container surfaces/appliance tops.
- When you go to a closed container, open it on arrival and read its contents. After that container visit, the next `go to` must be a non-container surface/appliance if one is available from the admissible list; otherwise choose a different container type. Do not take two consecutive container `go to` actions. On reaching either category, take the exact target immediately if it is visible.
- Continue this alternating pass until the exact target (or the required number of target instances for a multi-target task) is acquired, or until every available candidate location from the admissible list has been visited once.
applied_text_for_diagnostic_only.u2:
- After inspecting a receptacle that visibly lacks the exact target, do not choose `go to`/`open` on that same receptacle again; if the observation shows it is already open and empty, treat it as checked and choose a different admissible `go to` target instead.
- Do not cycle back and forth among the same small set of receptacles. If the last two observations show the same receptacle category, choose a different category from the admissible list, preferring one that does not appear in those two observations; if none exists, move to a different receptacle instance that is not shown as already open and empty.
- Treat a run of two steps whose observations both show opened, empty containers as a stuck-search signal: break it by moving to a different receptacle category, even if no target has yet been seen there.
